findings.title: Task 21 changes the `list_run_summaries` return type without updating its only caller before the Task 22 commit
findings.description:
Task 21 makes `list_run_summaries` return `RunListing(rows, unavailable)` and removes the per-run "pipeline unavailable" WARNING. Its only caller, `runs.py:27`, treats the result as a list of summaries and is not touched until Task 25. The Task 22 commit therefore lands with `sq runs list` broken or failing `pyright`, and with no unavailable-pipeline signal at all until Task 25 adds the summary line.

Fix: add a Task 21 step that adapts `runs.py` (and the `run_views` entry point) to read `listing.rows`. Either move the stderr summary line from Task 25 into Task 21, or say explicitly that the signal is absent between the two commits.

findings.title: Task 22a's seeding instruction collides with the keep-10 prune inside `init_run`, and its bound is thinner than stated
findings.description:
`init_run` calls `self.prune(pipeline_name)`, which deletes completed/failed runs beyond 10 per pipeline (`state.py:547-562`). Task 22a says only "seed a few hundred run-state files through `StateManager`" with a mix of completed and failed runs, then asserts the row count equals the seeded readable count. A junior implementer who seeds naively gets a count mismatch that is hard to diagnose. The 199 helpers already solve this (`tests/pipeline/run_listing_support.py:3-6`: begin all runs before finalizing any), but 22a does not point to them.

Fix:
- Tell the task to seed through `run_listing_support.begin`/`end` in begin-all-then-finalize order, or spread runs across pipeline names.
- Give the file count as a named constant; "a few hundred" is not a number.
- Reword "generous enough for CI jitter": the design's only measurement is 0.67 s for 188 runs for the whole CLI, so `MAX_LISTING_S = 1.0` has about 1.5× headroom at best, on shared runners across two Python versions.

findings.title: No task logs the run-id for an unknown process check
findings.description:
The design requires the unknown-PID case to be "logged at WARNING with the run-id and PID" (the error table at line 373 repeats it as "WARNING naming run and PID"). Task 9 logs the PID only and defers the run-id to "the caller that has it". None of the callers' tasks (19 wait, 21 listing, 33 prune) includes that log, and Task 10 asserts only the PID warning.

Fix: have `assess_liveness`, which holds the `RunState`, emit the WARNING with run-id and PID when `process_alive` returns `None`, and assert it in Task 10. One implementation point covers all three consumers.

findings.title: Spike outcome handling: a stop the design already resolves, and an unverifiable success criterion in Task 16
findings.description:
Task 2 says to stop and ask the Project Manager if no `ResultMessage` arrives after `interrupt()`. The design already decides that case (lines 621 and 261): the fallback is "always mark unusable", the step fails, and the design is updated. The stop is unnecessary and halts the slice on a planned branch.

Task 16's only success line (line 243), "adjust to the Task 2 spike findings if they differ from the design", is not checkable.

Fix:
- Replace the Task 2 stop with: record the finding, update the design's risk section, and implement Task 16 as always-unusable.
- Give Task 16 concrete criteria: usable when interrupt and drain complete; `unusable_reason` set and ERROR logged otherwise; `DispatchStalledError` raised in both cases.
- The D5 stop (line 59-60) is a real design fork (a per-run lock). If it is kept, express it as a `BLOCKED:` line, not an ask.

findings.title: Task 39 does not assert exit 1 for a failed deletion at the CLI level
findings.description: D9 says "The command exits 1 if any deletion failed". Task 37 covers the failed count in `apply_prune` and Task 38 implements the exit code, but Task 39 lists exit 1 only for the live-run refusal. One more case in Task 39 would close it.

findings.title: Task 42 adds a test seed helper inside a `docs:` commit, after the walkthrough it supports
findings.description: The seed helper under `tests/pipeline/` (orphan, stale, unowned, gone and junk runs) is code and would be committed as `docs: record slice 174 verification`. The same fixtures are needed by Tasks 22 and 39. Creating the helper in Task 22 as an extension of `run_listing_support.py` puts it in a `feat`/`test` commit and avoids duplicate seeding logic.
